question: If I-know-the-pot holds no difference, what of the pot appearing to me?
premises: Therefore in I-know-the-pot there is no difference at all.
But surely, this pot appears to me, so difference does manifest.
Not so, for the knower this very pot is Śiva, just so.
inference: The appearing difference is itself Śiva for the knower, holding non-difference.
uncertainties: Speaker shifts between objector and reply presumed.
plain_english: Therefore in 'I know the pot' there is no difference at all. But surely — 'this pot appears to me' — difference does manifest! Not so — for him this very pot is Śiva, just so.
